cards.panel:
L7
Verb families and infinitives
cards.prompt:
Identify the infinitive:
to work / I work
cards.meaning: The infinitive names an action without saying who does it.
cards.pattern: lavorare names the action; lavoro says who: I work. A verb can express an action, an event or a state.

cards.panel:
L7
Verb families and infinitives
cards.prompt:
Name the verb family:
lavorare · mangiare · parlare
cards.pattern: Look at the last three letters of each infinitive. Full present-tense practice in this lesson focuses on regular -ARE verbs.

cards.panel:
L7
Verb families and infinitives
cards.prompt:
Name the verb family:
vivere · vedere · leggere · scrivere
cards.pattern: vivere = to live; vedere = to see; leggere = to read; scrivere = to write. Recognise these infinitives here; their full conjugations are not introduced in this lesson.
cards.clarification: The minutes and table use vivere; slide 9 uses vedere. Both belong to -ERE, so both are retained.

cards.panel:
L7
Verb families and infinitives
cards.prompt:
Name the verb family:
dormire · aprire · finire
cards.pattern: dormire = to sleep; aprire = to open; finire = to finish. These are recognition examples, not a lesson in all their present forms.

cards.clarification:
How do I read the IPA? ˈ comes before the stressed syllable. ɛ / e and ɔ / o show open / closed vowels. ɲ is like Italian gn; ʎ is the Italian gli sound; tʃ is like ch in cheese; dʒ is like j in jam. Tap or roll Italian r. Hold doubled consonants slightly longer.

The English-friendly line is an approximate speaking aid. Capitals mark stress. These are careful-speech guides, not recorded audio.
